title: Yeh Prem Mol Liya Opens Near Rs 4 Crore, Barjatya's Second-Biggest Opening
excerpt: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari's Hindi family drama edges its Friday clash with Gunmaaster G9 as trackers put day one between Rs 3.67 crore and Rs 4 crore net.
body:
• Sooraj Barjatya's Yeh Prem Mol Liya, starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari, opened on Friday, November 27, with trade estimates of Rs 3.67-4 crore net in India.
  • Bollywood Hungama counted 145,309 tickets across 6,873 shows at 9.99% occupancy; Sacnilk's figures, carried by Koimoi, put the day at Rs 4 crore net and Rs 4.70 crore gross across 7,251 shows.
  • The opening is the second-biggest of Barjatya's career, behind only Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (Rs 40.35 crore), and ranks fourth among Sharvari's openers and tenth among Khurrana's.
  • The Hindi family drama beat its Friday clash rival Gunmaaster G9 (Rs 3.65 crore net, Sacnilk) while Ramayana: Part 1 continues its dominant run; the weekend trend now decides the film's course.

Sooraj Barjatya's return to the family drama he is known for has opened to a modest but milestone-marked first day. Yeh Prem Mol Liya, a Hindi romantic family drama starring Ayushmann Khurrana as Prem Mishra and Sharvari as Purva Solanki, collected an estimated Rs 3.67 crore net in India on Friday, November 27, according to Bollywood Hungama, which counted 145,309 tickets sold across 6,873 shows in 565 reported cities, at an overall occupancy of 9.99%. Sacnilk's tracking, reported by Koimoi, put the opening higher, at Rs 4 crore net and Rs 4.70 crore gross across 7,251 shows, with footfalls of about 1.89 lakh. All opening-day figures are trade estimates and the trackers differ; the film's own producers have not published a number.

Where the money came from

Maharashtra was the film's biggest market, contributing Rs 99.22 lakh net from 34,984 tickets, Bollywood Hungama reported, followed by the National Capital Region at Rs 66.11 lakh and Gujarat at Rs 33.27 lakh. The two regions together accounted for nearly 45% of the opening day. PVR was the largest chain contributor at Rs 1.16 crore net, with INOX adding Rs 73.88 lakh; together the two chains delivered about 52% of collections. The film had crossed Rs 1 crore in advance bookings before release, selling 43,622 tickets.

A clash, and a shadow

The Rajshri Productions and Mahaveer Jain Films presentation did not have the day to itself. It opened against Emraan Hashmi and Genelia Deshmukh's Gunmaaster G9, which Sacnilk estimated at Rs 3.65 crore net and Rs 4.30 crore gross — a narrower gap than the show counts suggest, since Yeh Prem Mol Liya earned its lead from fewer shows. Both films are also playing in the shadow of Ramayana: Part 1, which remains the dominant title in theatres three weeks into its run.

Milestones in the fine print

Measured against careers rather than the market, the opening travels well. At Rs 4 crore it is the second-biggest opening of Barjatya's directorial career, more than double his previous film Uunchai (Rs 1.81 crore) and behind only Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (Rs 40.35 crore). For Sharvari it ranks fourth, behind Alpha (Rs 9.25 crore), Vedaa (Rs 6.75 crore) and Munjya (Rs 4.21 crore). For Khurrana it enters his top ten openers at number ten. The ensemble cast includes Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa, Saumya Tandon, Shaad Randhawa and Swanand Kirkire.

Family dramas of this kind live or die on weekend word of mouth rather than opening-day scale, and trade reports describe the film picking up from morning shows into the evening. Saturday and Sunday growth — and how much of the audience Ramayana: Part 1 leaves behind — will decide whether the milestones become a run.
